Loan Origination Parity · UK unsecured personal loans

One specification. Four surfaces. The same answers.

One Gherkin store and one Serenity/JS Screenplay harness drive the same lending engine four ways: in-process, over REST, through an Angular SPA and through a Next.js backend-for-frontend. CI fails the build if any surface passes a different set of scenarios, or passes them with different step text.

Bars show reach by folder: domain rules · workflows · UI only. The core engine has no HTTP or UI, so it runs the domain rules; the API adds workflows; the browser surfaces run everything (DR-006).

02 · Screenplay

Same step, four surfaces

The step definition and the task are shared. Only the ability underneath changes, and step definitions are not allowed to know which one they have: the parity gate rejects any that mention a surface.

Gherkin · maker-checker.feature
When Sam approves the application
Step definition · shared
When('{actor} approves the application', (name) =>
  actorCalled(name).attemptsTo(CarryOut.the('approve')));
Ability · shared contract
abstract class OperateTheWorkbench extends Ability {
  approve(id: string) {
    return this.backend.approve(this.username, id);
  }
}

Tasks ask for OperateTheWorkbench.as(actor) and never learn which surface they are on.

03 · Security

Authorisation holds when the UI is bypassed

Hiding a button is never the only control. In these scenarios the actor forces a command the UI does not offer, straight at the server, and the server must refuse it with the right reason and leave the application unchanged (DR-010).

API

The command is sent directly to the REST endpoint as that member of staff.

Angular

The command goes to the API with the SPA's own session cookie, as a tampered browser would send it.

Next.js

A Server Action form captured from a permitted user is replayed as this user, without JavaScript (DR-018).

ScenarioActorForced commandServer refuses with APIAngularNext.js
The core engine enforces the same rules in-process; forcing is a UI-bypass test, so it runs where there is a UI or a wire.

05 · Proof the proof works

The gate fails when it should

A gate that never fails proves nothing. Every build of this page plants a one-step text change in a copy of one surface's report and runs the real gate on it. Scenario counts stay identical, so a count-only gate would pass. If the gate does not catch the change, the page is not built.
